title: Service energy and cost accounting metadata standard (v2)
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This page defines the company-wide standard for per-request energy and cost accounting metadata. The goal is to provide a consistent, compact envelope that services and proxies attach to requests and emitted telemetry so downstream billing, cost-optimization, SLO reconciliation, and sustainability metrics can reliably attribute spend and estimated energy consumption to tenants, models, and workload features.

This 2026 revision introduces cost_version=v2 and clarifies header propagation, typing, and privacy rules based on the 2025 rollout learnings.

Why this standard matters

- Unifies cost attribution across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Enables low-latency routing decisions using cost hints without leaking raw pricing data.
- Provides the data foundation for chargeback, forecast, and energy-conscious routing features.
- Supports audits and compliance with per-tenant retention and redaction policies.

Goals and constraints

1. Keep the per-request envelope small (<= 3KB) to avoid adding significant network or serialization overhead.
2. Include stable, well-documented keys (snake_case) rather than free-form tags.
3. Ensure values are typed and bounded (e.g., currency amounts in micro-units; energy in millijoules).
4. Make the envelope forward-compatible: allow vendor-specific extensions under a reserved prefix.
5. Avoid embedding per-token usage details in the routing envelope; use async telemetry for high-granularity events.

Scope

- Applies to: edge proxies (edge-router), API gateway (api-gateway), inference routers (inference-router), runtime sidecars (runtime-sidecar), batch job submitters, and telemetry collectors.
- Does not mandate billing rates or conversion tables — those live in the billing service and are referenced by id.
- Includes both real-time headers for short-lived routing decisions and persisted JSON envelopes for telemetry records.

Metadata fields (canonical envelope)

Use the following canonical keys in the JSON envelope attached to telemetry events and the corresponding HTTP headers for routing. Types and example values are provided. Services must include the required fields; others are optional.

Notes (v2):
- Numeric fields MUST be emitted as JSON numbers in persisted telemetry. For headers, the base64 envelope must preserve types.
- tenant_id remains required for internal telemetry; for cross-team aggregate pipelines, use hashed_tenant_id and omit tenant_id.

| Field | Required | Type | Description | Example |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| request_id | yes | string | Global request UUID (trace-friendly). | "req_123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000" |
| tenant_id | yes* | string | Tenant (customer) identifier used for billing. *Required for internal telemetry; must be omitted in "public-aggregate" pipelines. | "acme-corp" |
| hashed_tenant_id | no | string | Stable, salted tenant hash for aggregate analytics. Required when tenant_id is omitted. | "ht_9f2a0c..." |
| model_id | yes | string | Canonical model identifier (catalog/model-hash). | "redwood/gptx-7b:2025-03-01" |
| deployment_id | no | string | Deployment or cluster identifier for private/dedicated installs. | "dep_priv_usw1_003" |
| estimated_energy_mJ | no | integer | Estimated energy consumed by request in millijoules (best-effort). | 4120 |
| compute_microdollars | no | integer | Estimated compute cost in micro-dollars (USD * 1e6). | 125000 |
| currency | no | string | ISO currency code for compute_microdollars when non-USD (rare; telemetry-only). | "USD" |
| cost_version | yes | string | Version of the cost-accounting envelope schema (v1, v2...). | "v2" |
| pricing_ref_id | no | string | Billing service reference to the pricing table used (opaque id). | "price-table-prod-2026-01" |
| priority_class | no | string | One of: realtime, interactive, batch, bulk. Used for routing decisions. | "interactive" |
| cache_hit | no | boolean | True if the request was served from a cache (impacts cost). | true |
| gpu_tier | no | string | GPU tier hint (e.g., a100-80gb, h100-80gb, b200-80gb). | "h100-80gb" |
| inference_tokens_est | no | integer | Optional token estimate used for cost modeling (approx). | 120 |
| appended_by | yes | string | Service that appended/last-modified this envelope (service-name). | "inference-router" |
| routed_region | no | string | Region code used for routing (e.g., us-west1). | "us-west1" |
| cost_finalized | no | boolean | True if the envelope reflects finalized accounting (telemetry-only). | true |

Header mapping for real-time routing

- Preferred: X-RW-ACCT (base64-encoded JSON envelope).
- Minimal header set (when envelope is not available):
  - X-RW-REQ-ID
  - X-RW-TENANT (internal-only; must not be forwarded to customer-controlled hops)
  - X-RW-MODEL
  - X-RW-PRIORITY
  - X-RW-COST-VERSION

Header and forwarding rules (updated)

1. Runtime proxies must not forward tenant_id or pricing_ref_id outside Redwood-controlled networks. When traffic crosses a customer-controlled boundary, scrub X-RW-TENANT and any envelope fields containing tenant_id or pricing_ref_id.
2. pricing_ref_id MUST NOT appear in any externally-forwarded header. It may appear in internal telemetry.
3. If a service cannot safely attach headers (protocol limitation), it must attach the envelope only to telemetry.

Telemetry propagation and mutation rules

1. The first ingress service (edge-router or api-gateway) must create request_id and populate tenant_id and model_id.
2. Each service that materially changes estimated_energy_mJ or compute_microdollars must update appended_by to itself and emit a telemetry-only delta record (delta fields are telemetry-only and must never be included in routing headers).
3. runtime-sidecar may update compute_microdollars after final token counts; it must emit a separate telemetry record with final accounting and set cost_finalized=true.
4. If a proxy cannot compute estimated_energy_mJ, it must omit the field (do not set 0).

Schema versioning and compatibility

- Use the cost_version field to determine compatibility. Consumers must ignore unknown fields.
- v2 changes:
  - Clarifies numeric typing (JSON numbers in telemetry; preserve types in base64 envelope).
  - Adds hashed_tenant_id and deployment_id.
  - Deprecates the name X-RW-COST in favor of X-RW-ACCT (X-RW-COST is accepted until 2026-09-30).

SLOs and accuracy expectations (updated targets)

- Energy estimate accuracy: median absolute error <= 15% for production real-time estimates vs finalized telemetry for 95% of requests over a rolling 7-day window.
- Cost estimate accuracy: median absolute error <= 8% for compute_microdollars vs billing-service reconciliation for 99% of requests within 24 hours.
- Envelope propagation SLA: 99.95% of in-flight requests must carry either the minimal header set or the base64 envelope between edge-router/api-gateway and runtime-sidecar.

Storage, retention and redaction

- Telemetry envelopes stored in observability must omit tenant_id for analytics buckets labeled "public-aggregate". Use hashed_tenant_id when sending to cross-team aggregate pipelines.
- Raw envelopes with tenant_id and pricing_ref_id are PII-adjacent; retention default is 120 days unless tenant contract requires longer retention.
- For privacy-sensitive tenants, support redaction at ingress: redact_fields=["pricing_ref_id","estimated_energy_mJ"].

Rollout plan (recommended)

1. Week 0: Publish spec and unit tests in infra-standards repository; publish decoder for X-RW-ACCT.
2. Week 2: edge-router and api-gateway generate minimal headers and X-RW-ACCT. Keep emitting X-RW-COST for backward compatibility.
3. Week 4: inference-router and runtime-sidecar adopt v2 mutation rules and emit finalized telemetry with cost_finalized=true.
4. Week 6: billing-service consumes finalized telemetry and runs reconciliation; enforce updated accuracy metrics.
5. Week 8: Enable opt-in energy-based routing experiments for a small percentage of traffic (5%) using estimated_energy_mJ.

Validation and testing

- Unit test: schema validator that rejects envelopes with wrong types or missing required fields for the declared cost_version.
- Integration test: synthetic workload where compute_microdollars from runtime matches the billing-service computed microdollars within <8%.
- Smoke test: request roundtrip through edge -> runtime -> telemetry collector must include X-RW-REQ-ID and the envelope in the final event.

Example envelopes

Minimal header-encoded JSON (for routing):

X-RW-ACCT: eyAicmVxdWVzdF9pZCI6ICJyZXFfMTIzZSIsICJ0ZW5hbnRfaWQiOiAiYWNtZSIsICJtb2RlbF9pZCI6ICJyZWR3b29kL2dwdHgtN2I6MjAyNS0wMy0wMSIsICJjb3N0X3ZlcnNpb24iOiAidjIiLCAicHJpb3JpdHlfY2xhc3MiOiAiaW50ZXJhY3RpdmUiIH0=

Example telemetry JSON envelope (persisted):

{
  "request_id": "req_123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp",
  "model_id": "redwood/gptx-7b:2025-03-01",
  "estimated_energy_mJ": 4120,
  "compute_microdollars": 125000,
  "cost_version": "v2",
  "pricing_ref_id": "price-table-prod-2026-01",
  "priority_class": "interactive",
  "appended_by": "runtime-sidecar",
  "routed_region": "us-west1",
  "cost_finalized": true
}

Operational runbook snippets

- Problem: Missing tenant_id in envelopes for a subset of traffic.
  1. Check edge-router logs for header generation failures (service: edge-router, log key: cost-envelope-generation).
  2. Validate ingress auth middleware configuration: ensure tenant extraction rules are up-to-date.
  3. If using hashed_tenant_id fallback, verify the target pipeline is "public-aggregate" and that tenant_id is intentionally omitted.

- Problem: compute_microdollars differs from billing-service by > 15% (daily reconcile).
  1. Pull a sample of requests with request_id and compare runtime token counts vs billing charge pipeline.
  2. Verify pricing_ref_id mapping in billing-service and whether a new price-table was rolled without updating pricing_ref_id.
  3. Temporarily mark the envelope with telemetry-only debug fields (e.g., cost_override_reason="investigation") and ensure they do not appear in headers.

Governance and ownership

- Spec owner: Eng Infra Standards (primary: Aisha Kapoor; delegate for observability alignment: Evelyn Chen).
- Implementation owners: edge-router (team: eng-platform), inference-router (team: eng-serving-runtime), runtime-sidecar (team: eng-private-deployments), telemetry collector (team: eng-observability).
- Review cadence: Quarterly review or when cost_version increments.

Backwards compatibility guidance

- Producer-first approach: when introducing new fields, producers may emit them flagged as optional. Consumers must tolerate absent fields.
- Deprecation: announce deprecation of a key at least 8 weeks prior and publish a migration playbook.
- Header deprecation: X-RW-COST is deprecated in favor of X-RW-ACCT; dual-emit until 2026-09-30.

Open questions and future work

- Integrate energy models that use hardware telemetry (PState/PMU) for improved estimated_energy_mJ accuracy.
- Standardize hashed_tenant_id algorithm and key rotation guidance for cross-tenant analytics with privacy guarantees.
- Add support for per-region pricing overrides without increasing header cardinality.

Appendix: CLI validator example

# Validate an envelope file
cat envelope.json | python -m rw_cost_validator --schema v2 --check-types

Exit codes:
- 0: valid
- 1: schema error
- 2: missing required field

If you have questions or need exceptions for a specific private deployment, open a request in #eng-infra-standards and tag the spec owner.
